entirety with Councilmembers Ayala, Ramirez, and Valencia, Vice Mayor Rios, and Mayor

M. Alvarez-Glasman, City Attorney; and Camille Moreno, Assistant City Clerk.

followed by the flag salute, led by Allison Alexis Rodas, Moffit Elementary School.

in closed session.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Mayor Perez welcomed everyone to the meeting; thanked the California Contract Cities
for hosting a teleconference with Los Angeles County first responders to assist local cities
with El Niño storm preparations; reported on her attendance at the Norwalk Chamber of
Commerce After Hours Mixer, the Southeast Academy 9/11 Ceremony, the Norwalk High
School Civic Learning Award Ceremony, where Norwalk High School placed 1st in the
state, receiving the award from California Chief Justice Patricia Guerrero; announced that
the Taste and State of the City event will take place on October 16, at the Norwalk Arts
and Sports Complex; and the annual Veterans Day Ceremony will be held at the Norwalk
Sports Complex, November 11; she requested Levy Sun, Communications Director, post
and share flyers for both events; and indicated the meeting would be adjourned in memory
of Karla Butler, former Norwalk Chamber of Commerce Board Member. Vice Mayor Rios
reported on her attendance at the Norwalk High School Civic Learning Award Ceremony,
the Ribbon Cutting for Shanti Glow Yoga, the Gateway Cities 2026 Conference & Retreat;
and announced that the Southeast Area Animal Control Authority is hosting a pet adoption
special this month. Councilmember Valencia reported on her attendance at the Norwalk
Lions Club 80th Anniversary; held a meeting with a City of Whittier Councilmember to
discuss various topics; wished everyone a happy Central American Independence Day
and a happy Mexican Independence Day; and invited all to attend the Quarter Mania
event on October 10, at Saint Francis Episcopal Church. Councilmember Ayala thanked
Rita Ruiz, Director of Public Safety, and Noe Garcia, Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department

Background:

On March 10, 2021, President Biden signed the American Rescue Plan Act (“ARPA”) which
included State and Local Fiscal Recovery (“SLRF”) funds to support state and local governments
as they faced the impacts of the unprecedented COVID-19 pandemic. The City was allocated
$28,046,746 in ARPA funding, all of which was obligated toward eligible uses in accordance with
U.S. Department of the Treasury requirements as of December 31, 2024.

The City allocated ARPA funding across 26 eligible projects developed to address community and
operational needs consistent with ARPA regulations. Three projects have been completed under
budget, leaving $490,694 available for re-obligation towards other eligible ARPA projects.

Project No. 1.7C4219 - Website Enhancements:

Project No. 1.7C4219 – Website Enhancements was timely obligated through an agreement with
Revize LLC and was completed under budget, leaving $1,060 in ARPA funding available for re-
obligation to another active ARPA project.

Project No. 2.361219 – Aid to Impacted Industry Signage:

Project No. 2.361219 – Aid to Impacted Industry Signage was timely obligated through an Inter-
Agency Memorandum of Understanding (“MOU”) with the Community Development Department,
approved by the City Council in December 2024.

The project was established to upgrade and enhance wayfinding signage around the Norwalk
Entertainment Center in response to impacts associated with the COVID-19 public health
emergency. Due to ongoing construction in the area and the December 31, 2026 expenditure
deadline for ARPA funds, $149,634 remains available for re-obligation to other active ARPA
projects.

If approved, an amendment to the Inter-Agency MOU with the Community Development
Department will be required to reflect the revised ARPA project budget.

Viatron Systems Inc. The project was established to scan and digitize various City records and
documents for retention and improved accessibility.

The project is anticipated to be completed under budget, leaving $340,000 in ARPA funding
available for re-obligation to other active ARPA projects. If approved, an amendment to the

Project No. 1.7C5219 Cable Program Equipment Upgrade was timely obligated by the
December 31, 2024 obligation deadline through an Inter-Agency MOU with the Communications
& Public Affairs Department approved by the City Council in December 2024. The project was
established to obtain equipment and make upgrades to the City's Cable TV infrastructure to
enhance streaming capabilities.

To facilitate the timely expenditure of ARPA funds and provide flexibility to obtain additional minor
equipment necessary to complete the project, staff is proposing to re-obligate $1,060 in remaining
funding from Project No. 1.7C4219 Website Enhancements to Project No. 1.7C5219 Cable
Program Equipment Upgrade. If approved, an amendment to the Inter-Agency MOU with the

SUBJECT: ORDINANCE NO. 26-1769 - SALARY ADJUSTMENT FOR COUNCILMEMBERS
  UPON COMMENCEMENT OF NEW TERMS OF OFFICE

Background:

Effective January 1, 2024, California Government Code §36516 was amended to allow for the
first significant change in city council salary structures since 1984, now linking maximum pay to
city population. Under this new law, cities may increase city council salaries either by population
or by up to 5% annually. Norwalk falls into the 75,000-150,000 population category which allows
for a salary increase up to and including $1,900 per month.

In accordance with Government Code §36516.5, increases are prohibited from applying to a
council member during the council member’s term of office. It does, however, allow for all council
members to receive the increase when one or more members are sworn in to begin their new
term of office. Therefore, any increase would not become effective until after the certification of
the 2026 municipal election. Future adjustments may be made for inflation of up to the maximum
amount allowable based on population following the same percentage, but they cannot be
enacted without bringing an item back to City Council for consideration.

The City Council last received an increase to salary in 2007 following certification of the General
Municipal Election. At that time, the salary was adjusted to $951.91 per month. The proposed
new monthly salary is $1,900. If approved, it will become effective once the 2026 election is
certified.

Fiscal Impact:

The City Council salary will be included in the Fiscal Year 2026/27 budget. The increase for
roughly six months of this fiscal year will total approximately $28,440.90.

Background:

The City Hall Reception Improvement Project (“Project”) will replace the existing City Hall
Entrance and Information Center with a modern reception area that incorporates a Public Safety
Office. The Project is part of the City’s ongoing efforts to improve safety, security, functionality,
and the overall appearance of City Hall entrance and reception area.

The project is planned in preparation for The Walk project, located just outside City Hall, which
will feature housing and retail and is expected to increase activity and visitor traffic.
Improvements will create a more welcoming and comfortable space for visitors, enhance
American with Disabilities Act accessibility, and strengthen visitor management through
improved access controls.
The proposed improvements focus on renovating the existing City Hall entrance to provide a
more secure and functional space for employees and members of the public. The Project
generally includes modifications to the reception area and entrance, security-related
improvements, associated building improvements, and new furnishings.
On August 29, 2024, City Council awarded a professional services agreement to VCA Code to
provide design services for the Project. As the design progressed, staff evaluated available
cooperative purchasing contracts to facilitate implementation of the project and identified

In accordance with Norwalk Municipal Code Section 3.16.070(C), the City may utilize joint or
cooperative purchasing programs for the purchase of eligible supplies, materials, equipment,
and nonprofessional services. In addition, Public Contract Code Section 10298 authorizes Cities
to contract with California Multiple Award Schedule (“CMAS”) suppliers without further
competitive bidding, provided that the products and services procured are within the scope of a
supplier's CMAS contract. CMAS is a government agency service cooperative that provides
cooperative purchasing opportunities that allow public agencies to utilize established,
competitively procured contracts for eligible goods and services. Utilizing these cooperative
purchasing contracts streamlines the procurement process and provides access to established
contract pricing.

Staff determined that utilizing the applicable contract provides an efficient procurement method
for the Project and will allow the construction improvements to proceed in coordination with the
Project schedule.

For the construction component, staff obtained a proposal from KYA Services, LLC, (“KYA”)
utilizing California Multiple Award Schedule (“CMAS”) Contract No. 4-20-78-0089C. The
proposed work includes construction and installation of the improvements associated with the
City Hall reception area. Staff conducted a review of KYA’s qualifications, including verification
of the contractor’s California State License Board (“CSLB”) license, Department of Industrial
Relations (“DIR”) registration, State and Federal debarment status, and applicable CMAS
contract requirements. Based on the findings of the review, staff recommend awarding a contract
to KYA utilizing the CMAS contract for the construction and installation of the City Hall reception
improvements.

For the furniture and security components of the Project, the City will utilize KYA Services, LLC
and its subsidiary, TLS Choice, LLC, through CivicBuys under Arvin Union School District
Contract No. 000-6964. The cooperative purchasing contract will be utilized for the procurement
and installation of furniture, furnishings, security screening equipment, and related
improvements necessary to complete the City Hall reception area. Utilizing the cooperative
purchasing contract provides access to established contract pricing and allows the City to
coordinate these improvements within the overall Project schedule.

As the project enters the construction phase, staff now recommend entering into Amendment
No. 4 with VCA Code to provide additional design support services. The services will include
attending construction meetings, responding to contractor requests for information and
submittals, and preparation of as-built plans upon project completion.

City Council hereby finds that the proposed Project is categorically exempted pursuant to the
California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) Guidelines Section 15300.2. The Project is
